bull.b: A substantial cash reserve combined with no debt gives NovaBridge flexibility to fund important clinical milestones without immediate balance-sheet leverage. The stated runway through a potential 2028 interim readout supports sustained development execution and reduces near-term solvency pressure.

Givastomig has progressed from early clinical testing toward registrational development, supported by durable efficacy signals, manageable reported safety, Fast Track status and FDA protocol alignment. This combination improves the program's development clarity and potential strategic relevance.

Progress across VIS-101 and the broader Visara portfolio gives NovaBridge more than one potential value-creation pathway. A developing ophthalmology franchise can diversify reliance on givastomig and create additional partnering or development opportunities over time.

bear.b: NovaBridge has not established a stable revenue base and remains materially unprofitable after several years of recurring losses. Until clinical programs produce commercial or partnership receipts, financial performance will remain dependent on advancing assets rather than internally generated operating earnings.

bear.t: Ongoing Cash Burn And Financing Dependence
bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the company continues to consume capital while progressing its pipeline. Even with substantial liquidity, the need for further financing to begin Phase III creates execution uncertainty and could constrain development timing or shareholder returns.

Givastomig must establish meaningful differentiation in a rapidly developing CLDN18.2 field that includes several therapeutic modalities and validated competitors. Competitive pressure could affect trial positioning, regulatory expectations, partnering leverage and eventual adoption even if clinical results remain positive.
